title: IQM Announces Zero-Downtime Upgrade Program for Halocene Product Line Scaling Past 1,000 Qubits - Quantum Computing Report
gist: IQM launched a zero-downtime on-prem upgrade program for its Halocene QEC product line, migrating HPC and enterprise customers from a 150-qubit processor to future 1,000+ qubit systems by installing new units alongside old ones, built on NVIDIA CUDA-Q Logical and NVQLink; no delivery dates or logical-qubit specs were disclosed for the 1,000-qubit milestone.

insights.claim: IQM Quantum Computers unveiled at SC26 an on-premises upgrade program for its Halocene quantum error-correction product line, defining a hardware migration path from a 150-qubit processor to future systems exceeding 1,000 qubits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Upgrade-path commitments reduce obsolescence risk for HPC buyers and can lock in recurring hardware revenue.

insights.claim: Under IQM's Halocene deployment model, each next-generation unit is installed and commissioned alongside the existing system before the old hardware is decommissioned, maintaining continuity across software toolchains, Slurm-based schedulers and GPU interconnects.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Zero-downtime migration is a service differentiator that could drive multi-generation customer relationships.

insights.claim: IQM has not disclosed target delivery dates or logical-qubit specifications for the 1,000-qubit Halocene milestone.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The roadmap lacks hard commitments; investors should discount timing until dates are published.

insights.claim: IQM's Halocene architecture is built on an open, modular error-correction stack integrated with NVIDIA CUDA-Q Logical and real-time QEC decoding over NVIDIA NVQLink, letting customers pair local QPUs with existing CPU and GPU clusters for hybrid AI and simulation while keeping data on site.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: NVIDIA's NVQLink is becoming a standard QPU-GPU interconnect for QEC decoding, reinforcing NVIDIA's position in quantum.

insights.claim: IQM's Halocene logical-qubit roadmap, first introduced in November 2025, was selected by the LUMI AI Factory coordinated by CSC to deploy the LUMI-IQ superconducting system alongside the upcoming LUMI-AI supercomputer.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Anchor European supercomputing customer validates Halocene commercially.

insights.claim: IQM has completed 10 supercomputing integrations since 2021, including multi-generation upgrades at Finland's VTT (from 5 to 53 qubits) and four systems at Germany's Leibniz Supercomputing Centre (LRZ), including the Euro-Q-Exa system.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Track record of upgrades makes IQM's on-prem HPC positioning credible versus cloud-first competitors.
